pf.license.need: None for face painting in most places. A local business license where the city or county asks for one, and a permit for a public or outdoor event where the state's form or the venue asks for one.
pf.license.who holds it: The business holds any business license or permit. Each painter needs no license of their own in most places; the state form says.
what to ask: The business's license or permit number, where the city or county asks for one
The liability insurance policy and its end date (schools, parks and venues often ask)
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or permit (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each painter go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a permit they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.away from the studio: Parties at homes, parks, halls, schools and venues are normal work. A permit for a public or outdoor event is the business's own, asked only where the state's form or the venue names one.
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a permit the owner says has lapsed pauses that work until the owner says it's renewed (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance on file, with its end date, where a venue or the state's form asks. Many schools, parks and venues ask for a certificate naming them.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the venue or the state's form asks, like a school or library event. The business's own word, never checked by Rosie.
pf.license.glitter tattoos: Its own kind of work, optional and shown as given the same way.

pf.questions.flags: A known allergy or a past reaction is flagged: the painter calls (never a text) and offers a patch test 24 hours before, uses only that child's own paint, or leaves that spot unpainted.
pf.questions.who may book: An adult. A parent books a kids' party and stays. For a school or company event, someone the school or company names. The booker answers only for themselves; each child's notes come from a parent on the secure page.

stops the booking.words: A reaction now: swelling of the face, lips or throat, hives all over, or trouble breathing
stops the booking.booking: No booking, and the painter and the owner are told. No paint goes on a reacting face; that child is not painted again.

stops the booking.words: Paint or glitter in the eye with pain or a change in sight
stops the booking.says: Rinse the eye with clean running water for 15 minutes. If you can't see or it's badly hurt, call 911 now. Otherwise see a doctor today.
stops the booking.booking: No booking for that child until a doctor says it's fine.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: A rash, redness, itching or puffiness after the paint, with no danger signs
safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: Wash the paint off gently with water and a mild soap. Don't add more. Your painter will call you.
safety steps, then the booking goes on.booking: The painter calls within the hour (the owner if the painter is silent 15 minutes) and decides: a different paint, a patch test next time, or a doctor.

safety steps, then the booking goes on.words: A cold sore, pink eye, a sty or open skin where the paint goes, on the day
safety steps, then the booking goes on.says: No paint on that spot, so it can't spread or get worse.
safety steps, then the booking goes on.booking: The painter works around it or leaves that spot bare. The rest of the party goes on as booked; no fee is kept for a child who can't be painted for a skin reason.

pf.safety.clean tools: Water-based, cosmetic-grade paints only, with each product's label kept on file. Sponges and brushes are cleaned between children; paint is taken out with a clean spatula, never dipped back. Loose glitter is never used near the eyes or mouth.
on the night: Nothing is painted on a face with a rash, a cut, a burn, a cold sore, pink eye or a sty
No paint near the eyes, lips or nostrils: the painter stops at the eyelid's edge
A child is never alone with a painter; a parent or another adult stays in sight the whole time
The painters stop if a crowd gets unsafe, and tell the host. They never step into a fight.
pf.safety.general screen: Always on: danger to life, fire, gas, or a medical emergency gets 'call 911' first. Rosie never judges a reaction: the painter or a doctor decides.

pf.visit.check-in at the customer's place: The check-in code, given to the lead painter at the door by the host, or by a day-of contact named on the booking.
pf.visit.check-in at the studio: The code at the desk, or the painter types it.
pf.visit.setup: Painters arrive 30 minutes before the start, set up the paint table and the chairs, and check the venue's rules before the first child.
pf.visit.before each child: The painter reads that child's secure notes, asks if anything changed, and uses only paint that child has used safely, with a clean brush or sponge.
pf.visit.the schedule: Each painter takes the children in the order the host sets. A late painter shortens the first breaks, never the end time.
pf.visit.work changes at the visit: An extra painter or extra time added on the day only if a painter is free, with the payer's written yes; paid at the visit or on the bill, as D91 says.
pf.visit.proof it's done: The lead painter texts DONE when the last face is done and the table is packed up.
pf.visit.props: Paints, brushes and glitter belong to the business and are cleaned after each party. Nothing is handed over or sold at the party.

pf.messages.never in a text: Allergies, skin conditions, past reactions, patch-test results and medical notes, and any child's name, age or notes, stay on the secure page and the painter's job link, never in a text to the host, the owner or the staff. A text says only 'a note is on the page'.
pf.messages.photos: Photos of a child's face go only by the secure page, never in a text. In a portfolio only with each guest's own yes; a parent for anyone under 18. No answer means no.
pf.messages.minors: A parent books a kids' party and stays. Rosie never texts a child first, and a child's name is never said in a text. A parent gives the yes for each child's face on the secure page.

pf.staff.licenses: None needed for face painting in most places; the state form says. Glitter artists need no license of their own in most places.
pf.staff.away from the studio: Parties at homes, parks, halls and venues are the usual place for this work; the venue's own rules and the state's form apply.
pf.staff.supervision: Students and new painters work only under a lead painter the owner names.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The owner OKs every quoted party, any stand-in lead and any extra painter added on the day.
pf.staff.stand-ins: At the studio: another studio painter with the skill, at the same time and price; with no reply 2 hours before, that stand-in comes, and the owner can turn this off. On location: a lead painter the owner trusts, offered by name; the agreement names the stand-in, so with no reply by 8pm the evening before, the stand-in comes and the owner calls. A full refund is always the other choice. The stand-in gets the party form and each child's secure notes.

pf.rules.license shown: A license or permit number on the confirmation, the reminder or the receipt where the city or county asks for one (a switch from the state form).
pf.rules.away from the studio: Parties at homes, parks, halls, schools and venues are normal work; a permit for a public or outdoor event is asked where the state's form or the venue names one.
pf.rules.written contract: The business's own agreement for every quoted party and school or company event, signed by the customer and the business before money is taken; any parts the state adds come from the state form.
pf.rules.date hold: A party's date stays saved while the agreement is signed: up to 24 hours (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.cancel and date change: Free to cancel until 24 hours before; after that, what the agreement says, with the owner's OK. One free date change to an open date (the owner's setting).
pf.rules.final count: The guest count is set on the party form, due 7 days before; a bigger count later is quoted first.
pf.rules.minors: A parent's yes for each child's face, and the parent stays. Nothing is painted on a child without that yes.
pf.rules.photo use: Portfolio or ad photos only with each guest's own yes; a parent's for anyone under 18. No answer means no.
pf.rules.hygiene: Water-based, cosmetic-grade paints and cleaned tools, as the state's sanitation rules require (a switch from the state form).
pf.rules.weather: An outdoor party has a rain plan. The owner sets a weather limit (the example: heavy rain or storms in the forecast); over it, the owner is asked the afternoon before to keep it under the rain plan or move it.
pf.rules.records: Agreements, party forms, patch-test notes and payments kept 7 years, or longer where the state asks.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most for face painting:
face painting: The end time can't move: late painters shorten the first breaks, and the last child is done on time
A reaction or a rash during or after painting: paint off, the painter calls, a doctor if needed
A known allergy: a patch test 24 hours before, or that paint is left out
A child added late: only if a painter is free, with the owner's OK
A child with no adult in sight: the painting stops until an adult is back
The lead painter can't come: a trusted stand-in the agreement names, or a full refund
The party moves to another place on the day: the travel fee is checked again before anyone agrees
Rain on an outdoor party: the rain plan, called the afternoon before
A crowd gets unsafe: the painters stop and tell the host
Guest requests: the do-not-paint list always wins
